Round 2 · Implementation · Medium

Ticket #21 — Data Import Pipeline

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain an operations tool that receives a partner's already-decoded CSV rows as a list of dictionaries. Each partner ID identifies one stored customer record. The import should save valid independent rows and report errors by their 1-based row number, so an operator can correct the input without losing good rows.

Practice report

Start with an empty repository and post these rows through ImportRoutes.post:

[
    {"id": "a", "email": "a@x.test", "amount": True},
    {"id": "b", "email": "b@x.test", "amount": "4"},
]
Observation Current starter Expected
Accepted IDs ["a", "b"] ["b"]
Error row numbers [] [1]
Persisted records a with amount 1; b with amount 4 Only b with amount 4

The boolean is malformed input; it must not become a financial amount.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Accept a nonnegative integer amount supplied as an integer or a base-10 integer string. Reject booleans, floats, negative amounts, missing fields, blank trimmed IDs, and emails without @.
  • Trim IDs and emails and store emails in lowercase. Return accepted IDs and errors in input order, with the original 1-based row number for each error.
  • An invalid row changes no record; continue to save valid independent rows.
  • Within one batch, the first valid row for an ID wins. Report later duplicates without replacing it, and never overwrite a preexisting stored ID.
  • A non-list top-level body returns 400 without persistence effects. A list with errors returns 207; a fully accepted list returns 201.

Out of Scope

Work with parsed row dictionaries and the existing in-memory repository. Reading CSV bytes, file uploads, all-or-nothing batch transactions, and changing customer IDs are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Trace the two-row report through the route, parser, and store. Add mixed-batch cases with a float, bad email, duplicate ID, existing ID, and later valid row. Assert row numbers, normalized records, and preserved existing values.
